title: Launch Agent 7 sources its Operational Facilitator and Operational GovOps from a separate Executor Agent rather than staffing them itself
content:
Launch Agent 7's Executor Accord Primitive is `Active` (A.6.1.1.8.2.2.1.1.1) with a single Active Instance named Ozone. That Instance's one substantive parameter is a pointer: "The Operational Facilitator and Operational GovOps for Ozone are specified in A.6.1.2.2 - Operational Executor Agent Ozone" (A.6.1.1.8.2.2.1.2.1.1.1).

This is a separation-of-powers move expressed as document structure. Every consequential step in Launch Agent 7's own governance — alignment review, feasibility confirmation, triggering the vote, enacting the edit — is performed by the Operational Facilitator, and that Facilitator is defined in a *different* Agent's Artifact. Launch Agent 7 cannot redefine its own reviewer by editing its own document.

The Accord is also the unit of the relationship: it is an Operational Primitive with ongoing management (A.6.1.1.8.2.2.1.2.1.2 defines "the process for the ongoing management of the Ozone Instance"), not a one-time appointment. Executor services are therefore a live, revisable engagement between two Agents, with the Accord Instance as the contract record.

The trade-off is dependency: an Agent whose reviewer is external gains impartiality but loses self-sufficiency — if the Ozone Accord lapses or is suspended, the routine Root Edit path has no actor to run it.
description: The Executor Accord Primitive's Ozone Instance points at Operational Executor Agent Ozone for both roles, so the Prime Agent's governance operators live outside its own Artifact.
